predictions.title: Toronto +1.5 on the puck line against the Rangers
predictions.body: Selection: Toronto Maple Leafs +1.5 on the puck line against the New York Rangers at Scotiabank Arena. Toronto are 5-4-2 through eleven games, have scored 38 goals at 3.45 per game and conceded 34, and they beat San Jose 3-1 on 19 October. Auston Matthews has 8 goals and 18 points in eleven games on 33 shots, with William Nylander adding 6 goals and 15 points. The Rangers are 7-3-1 and beat Anaheim 5-2, so this line needs the Leafs to avoid a two-goal defeat rather than to win.
facts: Toronto record 5-4-2, 38 goals for, 34 against in 11 games
Toronto beat San Jose 3-1 on 19 October
Matthews 8 goals, 18 points, 33 shots; Nylander 6 goals, 15 points
predictions.model_note: Expected goals from the club rates: Toronto 2.82, Rangers 3.05. The model gives Toronto a 23.2% chance of winning by two or more, so +1.5 lands at 70.64% (fair -241).

predictions.title: San Jose to score two or more at Ottawa
predictions.selection_label: San Jose Sharks over 1.5 team goals
predictions.body: Selection: San Jose Sharks to score over 1.5 goals, meaning two or more, against the Ottawa Senators at Canadian Tire Centre. San Jose have 26 goals in ten games and Macklin Celebrini leads them with 5 goals, 9 assists and 14 points in eight appearances on 37 shots. The Sharks scored four in a 4-3 overtime win at Montreal on 20 October, a night after a 3-1 loss at Toronto, and Ottawa have conceded 24 goals in ten games, so two goals is a measured ask.

Sharks won 4-3 in overtime at Montreal on 20 October
Sharks lost 3-1 at Toronto on 19 October
Ottawa conceded 24 goals in 10 games (2.40 per game)
predictions.model_note: Sharks scoring rate is modelled at 2.50 goals; P(2 or more) = 71.27% on the independent Poisson line, a fair price of -248.

flags.title: The brief's two High rules only overlap in a 1.43-point window
flags.detail: A probability above 70% implies a fair price shorter than -233.33; a fair price no shorter than -250 implies a probability at or below 71.4286%. Obeying both at once leaves 70.00%-71.43%. 127 of the 600 priced selections clear 70%; seven sit inside the window; two carry complete evidence and are labelled High. The five in-window selections labelled Medium are listed on the High-confidence page with the reason each was capped.

flags.title: MLB prices use full-season run rates, not postseason inputs
flags.detail: Both World Series teams' rates come from 162 regular-season games. Starting pitchers, bullpen usage, park effects and postseason form are not modelled, so no MLB selection is labelled High and the caveat is printed on every MLB market block.

flags.title: NHL model has no goaltender, injury, rest or home-ice adjustment
flags.detail: The NHL line uses club goals for and against per game only. Goaltender starts, injuries, back-to-backs and home-ice advantage are absent, so every NHL price carries model risk that is not quantified here.

flags.detail: The model computes 71.48% for Anaheim +1.5, a fair price of -250.6, which rounds to -251 and is therefore outside the -250 floor. It is published as Medium rather than re-rounded into the band.

flags.title: Later World Series games are conditional
flags.detail: Games 2-6 are scheduled by MLB in advance; they are only played if the series continues. The feed returns status Scheduled, which is a schedule entry, not a guarantee that the game takes place. Their model prices carry that caveat.

flags.title: OLBG tip shares are votes, not probabilities
flags.detail: OLBG was used for discovery only. Its percentage next to a selection is the share of community tips, not a modelled chance, and it is never used as an input to a price.
